title: POC Landing: Collaborative Sprint Agenda & Slide Skeleton
summary: Working doc for a 1.5 day customer POC landing sprint. Includes a tight agenda, slide skeleton for customer-facing kickoff, facilitator cues, prework checklist and measurable acceptance criteria. Intended for SEs running rapid on-site or remote deployments where we need to validate performance, integration points, and success metrics within a short cadence.
audience: Solutions Engineers, Customer Success, Customer technical leads, Platform engineers
agenda: Day 0 (Prework) - deliver integration checklist and sample payloads (async): customer engineering completes access and sample data
Day 1 AM (2 hrs) - Kickoff + architecture alignment: 20m intros + goals, 40m current arch review and constraints, 60m data & privacy discussion
Day 1 PM (3 hrs) - Rapid deploy & smoke test: 45m infra staging, 60m model selection & config (batching, quant), 75m end-to-end smoke tests and latency checks
Day 2 AM (2.5 hrs) - Workloads & evals: 30m define evaluation prompts/metrics, 90m run evals (latency, throughput, quality), 30m triage failures
Day 2 Midday (60m) - Runbook + next steps: compile runbook, SLA proposal, prioritized backlog, follow-up ownership
Follow-up (asynchronous) - 2 week checkpoint with perf report and recommended optimization plan
slide_outline: Title slide: Customer name + POC dates + SE leads
Desired outcomes: 3 bullets (business outcome, performance target, integration milestone)
Scope & out-of-scope: short list, clear success criteria
Current architecture snapshot: systems, data flow, network constraints
Redwood landing approach: hosted vs dedicated vs private options (high level)
Deployment plan: infra steps, config knobs to test (batch size, prefix caching, quantization)
Acceptance tests & metrics: latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, error budget, quality checks
Risk & mitigations: e.g., rate limits, data privacy, model regressions, fallbacks
Immediate operational artifacts delivered: runbook, Kibana/console dashboard links, contact list
Next steps & timeline: handoff, production readiness checklist, commercial next steps
prework_checklist: Customer grants API keys / service account for staging project
Provide representative sample payloads (10-50 examples) and a small ground-truth set for evaluation
Confirm network egress rules / VPC peering window (list ports and windows)
List any regulated data that must remain on-prem or encrypted at rest
Customer identifies 2 technical contacts and one business sponsor
facilitation_notes: Tone: pragmatic, outcome-focused. Start each section by restating the outcome and timebox. Use whiteboard for architecture and for defining success criteria. Be explicit about what we will NOT do in the POC to avoid scope creep. Facilitation script highlights: (1) Kickoff: ask customer for top 2 worst-case failures in production — capture and propose immediate mitigation; (2) Deployment: remind group of rollback and snapshot points before any disruptive change; (3) Eval: run metrics live and narrate what each metric implies for user experience. Timeboxing guidance: call out mid-session check-ins (5 mins) to surface blockers. Recording: capture screenshots of console dashboards and save a short Loom of the end-to-end smoke test for asynchronous stakeholders.
roles_and_responsibilities: SE lead: overall agenda, deploy steps, config decisions
Integration engineer (customer): provide access, run local tests, reproduce issues
SRE/Platform engineer: assist with infra provisioning and networking
CS/AM: own success criteria and commercial follow-ups
acceptance_criteria: E2E latency: p95 <= 1.2x baseline or absolute < 600ms for targeted workflow
Throughput: sustained tokens/sec within 20% of target under demo load
Functional: model outputs meet business QA on the ground-truth sample (>= 85% pass rate on defined checks)
Operational: console shows tracing, cost estimator within expected budget, alerts wired to customer Slack/ops channel
common_pitfalls_and_mitigation: Missing sample data or mismatch of production shapes -> require synthetic generator and subset validation
Network egress blocked -> pre-validate firewall rules and provide test endpoints
Model quality drift during quantization -> run small A/B and keep FP32 fallback ready
Overly broad success criteria -> convert to measurable slices (latency/memory/quality per intent)
deliverables: Lightweight runbook (markdown) with step-by-step deploy + rollback
Performance snapshot (p50/p95, tokens/sec) and cost estimate
Short slide deck (10 slides) for exec recap
Issue log and prioritized backlog for production gates
follow_up_plan: Within 3 business days deliver runbook, perf snapshot, and a prioritized list of optimizations. Schedule a 2-week deep-dive to implement recommended quantization/batching changes and re-run E2E evals. For Dedicated/Private interest: include an FYI budget template and infra sizing baseline in follow-up packet.
notes_to_self: Keep one config parameter immutable during smoke tests to aid root-cause (e.g., keep batch-size constant while toggling quantization). For remote POCs, over-communicate exact times for network changes since timezone differences often delay tests.
estimated_time_budget: Total: 12 person-hours across SE/SRE/CS during 1.5 day sprint. Follow-ups ~8-16 person-hours depending on optimizations
